q_hi:
Comprehension:
Read the passage carefully and answer the following questions.

Fresco painting, derived from the Italian word fresco meaning "fresh," is a celebrated mural technique that involves applying water-based pigments to freshly laid lime plaster. The process begins with preparing the wall surface by spreading wet plaster, which must remain damp to absorb the pigments effectively. As the plaster dries, the pigments chemically bond with it, making the artwork a permanent part of the wall. This method, known as buon fresco, requires the artist to work swiftly and precisely, completing each section—called a "giornata" or "day’s work"—before the plaster sets. This technique reached its pinnacle during the Italian Renaissance, most notably through the work of Michelangelo. Though he considered himself primarily a sculptor, Michelangelo was commissioned by Pope Julius II to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, a project he undertook from 1508 to 1512. The ceiling features over 300 figures from the Book of Genesis, including the iconic Creation of Adam, which showcases his mastery of human anatomy and expressive composition. Michelangelo returned to the Sistine Chapel decades later to paint The Last Judgment on the altar wall (1536–1541), a dramatic and emotionally charged fresco that reflects his evolving style and deepening psychological insight. Despite his personal frustrations with the medium, Michelangelo’s frescoes remain monumental achievements in art history. His disciplined approach and visionary execution transformed the Sistine Chapel into a lasting testament to the power of fresco as both a technical and expressive form.
Identify the most appropriate title for the passage.
